title: The primorial exists in this kernel as a computable fold over minFac
statement: Nat.primorial n is the product of every prime p <= n, constructed as Nat.prodRangeIf (fun i => Nat.beq (Nat.minFac i) i) (fun i => i) (Nat.succ n) -- a fold over the predicate-restricted range [0, n], with no choice principle and no decidability instance. The predicate is minFac-based rather than isPrime-based (see F:nat-min-fac-eq-self-of-prime for why), and it admits i = 1: minFac 1 = 1 is Mathlib's own boundary convention, so 1 passes the test. It contributes the factor 1, the multiplicative identity, so the VALUE is still exactly the product over the primes -- which is a claim about the definition, checked by evaluation at n = 0..7 against the hand-computed 1, 1, 2, 6, 6, 30, 30, 210, and not by argument.

evidence.supports: Nat.primorial is admitted as a Definition of type Nat -> Nat, arity 1.
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example shape_search -- --name Nat.primorial --kind definition --expect 1
evidence.notes: `nat_theorem_inventory` lists THEOREMS and returns zero rows for a definition (CLAUDE.md's own warning, reproduced here: `nat_theorem_inventory primorial` printed the ten `primorial_*` theorems and not `Nat.primorial` itself), so the declaration is pinned through `shape_search --kind definition --expect 1`, whose exit status depends on the count. The same run reported `declarations=3222`, above the 3,050 floor, and `--name-like primorial` had reported ABSENT at `declarations=3207` before this lane wrote anything.

evidence.supports: Nat.primorial reduces to 1, 1, 2, 6, 6, 30, 30, 210 at n = 0..7, and is NOT def-eq to any of four named wrong formulas of the same type.
evidence.notes: The trusted gate cannot tell a Definition is wrong: every variant ruled out here also has type Nat -> Nat. The four negative controls name the specific wrong formula each excludes -- primorial 4 != 24 rules out a product over the whole range, primorial 7 != 30 rules out a `< n` bound instead of `<= n`, primorial 3 != 2 rules out a predicate admitting only 2, and primorial 2 != 1 rules out a predicate that is never true. n = 4 is the first COMPOSITE step and n = 7 the first place the inclusive bound is observable at a prime.

evidence.supports: The two defining equations are admitted and hold by Eq.refl; the successor equation is checked at a FREE variable, not at a numeral.
evidence.notes: A succ-equation that held only at literals would reduce on both sides and pass a numeral test while being useless to every induction downstream, so the check pushes a typed LocalDecl and goes through `infer_in`/`def_eq_in`. `Kernel::infer` builds an EMPTY LocalContext and would report `UnboundFVar` instead. The negative control is the UNCONDITIONAL `primorial (succ n) = primorial n * succ n`, which is true only at primes and is what dropping the Bool selector would produce.

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- the Nat environment admits no trusted declaration
evidence.notes: `the_primorial_shelf_is_admitted_and_axiom_free` asserts `Environment::contains` FIRST for each name -- and, for `Nat.primorial` itself, that the declaration kind is `Definition` and not `Theorem` -- before reading the footprint, because the footprint of an absent name is also empty.

provenance.source: construction authored in this repository; every evaluation value was hand-computed as the running product of 2, 3, 5, 7 before the definition was written. `shape_search --name-like primorial` reported ABSENT at declarations=3207, with `--name-like lcmupto --kind definition` as the same-kind positive control and `Nat.Finset.card_singleton` (merged the same morning) as the freshness control.

notes: Roadmap W3-11, ADR-1637. Deliberately NOT routed through `Nat.primeCounting`: five of the ten rows of the preregistered, never-scored held-out family `discrete-step-and-counting-bounds` are the `Nat.primeCounting` shelf, and a theorem about that constant publishes the mathematics the family's blindness depends on. A COUNT built on this file's predicate would be off by one at i = 1 and would need a `2 <= i` conjunct; a PRODUCT does not, which is one more reason the primorial and the counting function are kept apart here.
